name: Bento grid
description: A modular grid with fixed-height rows and dense packing: children declare both a column span and a row span, and the browser backfills gaps. For tile walls and bento sections where cards are deliberately different sizes. The fixed row height is what makes row spans predictable — in a normal row, rows are content-sized and a row span means nothing.

breakpointBehavior.behavior: 6 columns, 120px rows, dense packing. row-span-sm-* applies.
12 columns, 120px rows. row-span-md-* overrides row-span-lg-* in this range.
Inherits lg. The tiles grow with the container, not the row height.

classes.name: bento-grid
classes.purpose: Dense-packed modular grid with fixed row height.

classes.name: row-span-md-2
classes.purpose: Occupy two rows in the tablet range.

customProperties.name: --s2a-grid-row-height
customProperties.purpose: The fixed row height, 120px. The one number in the grid system that is not yet a token.

rules.statement: Rows are a fixed 120px, which is what makes a row span mean something.
Packing is dense, so a short tile backfills a hole left by a tall one instead of leaving a gap.
Row spans exist for the mobile range.
Row spans exist for the tablet range.
Row spans exist for the desktop range.
The row height should be a semantic token like every other dimension in the grid, not a literal in the stylesheet.

decisions.question: Should the 120px row height change per breakpoint? It is currently fixed at every range, so a two-row tile is 248px tall on a phone and on a 2560 display.
decisions.evidence: The Bento component and its visual eval pass at 120px today (10/10 within 8%), so this is a question about the general grid rather than a defect in the shipped component.

visualize.note: Tiles carry both a column span and a row span; the dense packing is visible where a small tile backfills.
